title: Shekere (gourd rattle)
summary: The shekere is a large dried gourd wrapped in a loose net of beads or seeds. Shaken, the beads rattle; touched with the fingertips they click sharply; struck on the base with the palm the gourd gives a deep, hollow bass. Skilled players toss and spin it to draw layered rhythms from the net.
howToPlay: Four places on the gourd are lit: Shake high on the neck, Slap and Roll on the belly, and Bass at the base.
A ring closes on a place when its stroke is due. Strike that place just as the ring meets the gourd.
Begin with the four-beat bead pulse, then try the twelve-pulse figure.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of West African gourd-rattle playing, not transcriptions.
heritageNote: The shekere comes from the music of the Yoruba people of West Africa and travelled to the Caribbean and Brazil, where gourd rattles of this kind still join drum ensembles.
